title: The Load-Bearing Drawer
logline: Quinn asks Barney for one drawer, and clearing it means dismantling an apartment engineered to get women out by breakfast. Quinn, it turns out, has been several moves ahead the whole time.
coldOpen: Kids, your Uncle Barney's apartment was engineered by the finest minds in New York for one purpose: getting women out of it before breakfast. Then Quinn asked for a drawer.

couch.line: A contractor named Hank. And a young architect who insisted the oven needed crown molding.

guests.name: Hank
guests.role: the soft-spoken contractor who built every anti-commitment feature in Barney's apartment, takes deep craftsman's pride in each one, and has been happily married for forty years

scenes.summary: Barney announces Quinn's drawer request, reveals his apartment's defense system; Marshall's drawer-less life is set up; Quinn calls Barney's bluff and sets a deadline; Lily volunteers to stall her for evil reasons.

beats.line: Guys. Code red. Quinn asked for a drawer.
Barney, that's wonderful! A drawer is the first chapter of a beautiful—
A drawer is a beachhead, Ted. Then it's a toothbrush. Then you're at her parents' cottage, losing a card game they made up.
So clear one out. You live alone in a penthouse. How hard can it be?
Lily, my apartment isn't an apartment. It's a machine. Every inch is engineered to get a woman out by seven a.m.
Behold. Eight years of research and development.
beats.title: The Apartment: Defensive Features
lines: The oven is cardboard. No breakfast.
The welcome mat is a scale.
Every clock runs four hours fast.

beats.line: Why is the welcome mat a scale?
If she weighs more than last time, she's smuggling in an overnight bag. The mat texts me.
And the clocks?
She wakes up, sees it's eleven, screams about work and flees. No goodbyes. No brunch.
That's monstrous.
That's genius.
At least you have drawers. I haven't had a drawer since 2009.
You have your briefcase, baby.
My socks live in my briefcase, Lily. I opened it in court today. The judge saw argyle.
How does a man lose every drawer in his own home?
Drawer creep. One sweater at a time, over four years. He thinks the drawers shrank.
They did shrink, Robin. It happens in humid buildings.
Babe! Hi! We were just discussing humidity.
Here's how this goes. You say, of course, babe. Then you do something insane.
Of course, babe.
Great. Tomorrow, seven o'clock. One empty drawer. A real one. I know about the fake ones.
I need a demolition crew. Ted, you're an architect. Robin, you're emotionally unavailable.
Finally. My skills are needed.
And I'll stall Quinn tomorrow.
Lily. You'd do that for me?
For you? No. I want front-row seats to both disasters.

scenes.summary: The crew tries to empty one drawer. Each drawer exposes another feature, Hank explains the system is load-bearing, Ted's crown molding is exposed, and Barney forbids the nightstand. The clocks lull them into thinking they have hours.

beats.line: The next day, Barney called in the man who built the place.
Mr. Stinson. Forty years happily married, and this apartment is still my favorite job.
Hank, I need you to un-build one drawer by seven.
Mr. Stinson. Nothing in this apartment is just one drawer.
Barney, why is the kitchen drawer full of envelopes?
Pre-signed goodbye letters. Last night was magical. The doorman will call you a cab.
Can I get a box of those?
Fine. We move the letters into the drawer by the couch.
Can't. That's the Antarctica drawer.
One-way tickets to a research station. I'm leaving tomorrow. I've been leaving tomorrow since 2005.
What would you even research?
Penguins, Ted. They mate for life. Somebody has to find out why.
Barney, this apartment is a crime against architecture.
Says the man who wanted crown molding on the oven.
It was a cardboard oven, Robin. It didn't have to look cardboard.
Marshall. You're four pounds heavy. Is that an overnight bag?
beats.title: Welcome Mat

messages.text: 4.2 lbs over last visit. Possible overnight bag.

beats.line: It's my socks, Barney. They're not staying over. They don't have anywhere to stay.
Every drawer in here is load-bearing. Empty one, the clocks reset. Reset the clocks, the Stormtrooper panics.
What does the Stormtrooper do?
Seven a.m. sharp, he tells her the building is being fumigated.
Honestly? That's beautiful. I keep a fake cat at my place. For excuses.
Robin, you have five real dogs.
The cat's for when the dogs aren't enough.
Hank. Drawers aren't load-bearing. I'm an architect.
Emotionally, Ted.
What about the nightstand in the bedroom?
Not that one!
What's in it?
Nothing.
Then it's perfect! It's already empty!
It's not empty, Ted. It's full of nothing. There's a difference.
Oh no. It's six-fifteen. She'll be here at seven!
Barney, your clocks run four hours fast. It's two-fifteen.
See? Even the clocks are on my side.

scenes.summary: Lily stalls Quinn, who has known about every trap since date three. Quinn coaches Lily on drawer economics, keeps her real plan secret, and reveals she reset Barney's clocks months ago, so the crew is out of time.

beats.line: Meanwhile, Lily had taken Quinn to the slowest restaurant in Manhattan.
And then the Fiero's horn went off by itself, at a funeral, during a blizzard—
Lily, that's the second time you've told me that story. It had a different funeral.
It's a living story. It grows.
You're stalling. It's fine. I know exactly what's waiting at that apartment.
Do you? Because the oven is cardboard.
I tried to preheat it on our third date. Small fire. Lovely smell.
And you stayed? What else do you know?
Everything. Including how you took every drawer from Marshall. Four years, one sweater at a time. Respect.
Thank you. Nobody ever appreciates the craft.
Give him one back. A man with one drawer will defend it forever. A man with zero starts browsing studio apartments.
Then why put Barney through all this? Just to watch him panic?
I don't want any drawer. I want to see if he gives me the right one.
There's a right one? Tell me. Tell me everything.
Lily, you keep secrets badly.
I keep them briefly. That's different.
Anyway, they think they have four hours. I set his clocks right in March. He still thinks they're fast.
Check, please! I need to see their faces!

scenes.summary: Quinn arrives right on time, beats the mat, and reveals she has been using the nightstand drawer for months. James's flashback shows Barney kept that one drawer trap-free from day one. Barney gives it to her properly; Quinn negotiates the oven away; Lily returns a drawer to Marshall.

beats.line: Good news. I built you a brand-new fifteenth drawer. Totally empty.
Hank, you beautiful man. What's the catch?
When she opens it, it plays a recording of your mother.
Tasteful. Relax, everybody. We have four whole hours.
Hi, babe. Seven o'clock.
Ted! You said we had four hours!
I did the math with the clocks I was given.
Your clocks are right, babe. I fixed them back in March.
But that means I've been four hours late to work every day since March.
Did anybody notice?
No.
Okay, but the mat says you weigh exactly what you always weigh. No overnight bag. Ever.
I'm a dancer, Barney. I hold the door frame. I've been bringing an overnight bag for months.
That's not how scales work.
It is with good upper-body strength.
For months? Then where have you been putting your—
Oh my god. The nightstand.
Toothbrush, spare tights and an emergency granola bar.
You found it.
Date three. Thirteen traps and one empty drawer. A man doesn't leave that by accident.
Kids, years later, your Uncle James told me how that drawer came to be.
Oven's done. Pure cardboard. Looks real from every angle.
Little brother, this isn't an apartment. It's an escape room for other people.
Every drawer gets a trap, Hank. Every single one.
The nightstand too?
Leave that one. In case somebody ever finds it.
You big softie.
Tell anyone and Hank builds a cardboard oven in your house.
Everything in here is built to make people leave. That drawer was the one thing I couldn't booby-trap.
So why didn't you just give it to me?
Because if I give it to somebody and they leave anyway, it's just a drawer again.
I'm not leaving, Barney. I just wanted you to hand it to me.
Quinn Garvey. Will you take my drawer?
Yes. Also, the oven goes.
The oven stays.
Hank, the oven goes.
That's the most romantic thing that's ever happened to furniture.
Marshmallow. I'm giving you a drawer back.
Lilypad!
It's under the sink. Behind the drain cleaner.
I'll take it! My socks are going to be so happy!
Great. I'm going home to hug my fake cat.
Kids, by Christmas Quinn had the drawer, the closet and naming rights to the Stormtrooper. The drawer was just her opening offer.
